quests.instruction: Scan the text for the detail you need, then answer.
quests.passage: Today at the Regent Cinema. Screen 1: Moonlight Harbour (2h 05m) at 1:20, 4:10, 6:45 and 9:15. Screen 2: The Last Orchard (1h 40m) at 2:00, 4:30 and 7:10, with a subtitled showing at 9:40. Screen 3: Paper Wings, a family film (1h 25m), at 11:00, 1:15 and 3:30 only. Tickets are half price before noon. No late entry once a film has started.
quests.question: When is the last showing of The Last Orchard?
quests.hint: Jump straight to the film's title and ignore the other screens.
quests.explanation: Scanning means going directly to the name you need. The 9:40 showing is subtitled but still a showing, and 9:15 belongs to a different film.

quests.instruction: Skim the text for the main idea, then answer.
quests.passage: Across the city, small gardens are appearing on rooftops, balconies and even old parking spaces. Residents say growing herbs and tomatoes gives them fresh food and a reason to meet neighbours. The council now offers free soil and seeds to groups that apply, hoping the idea will spread. Some experts warn that heavy planters need to be checked for safety, but most see the trend as good for both wellbeing and the environment.
quests.question: What is the general message of the text?
options: Rooftops are too dangerous for any kind of garden
Small urban gardens are spreading and bring benefits
The council wants to sell seeds to residents
Tomatoes grow best on balconies in the sun
quests.correctAnswer: Small urban gardens are spreading and bring benefits
quests.hint: Read the first and last sentences and let the middle confirm your idea.
quests.explanation: Skimming for the gist means noticing the overall direction. The safety warning is a minor point that most experts do not stress.

quests.instruction: Scan the text for the detail you need, then answer.
quests.passage: Rooms at the Bayfront Hotel: standard double, $110 per night; superior double with sea view, $145; family room sleeping four, $180; suite, $260. Breakfast is $12 per person and parking is $15 per night. Children under six stay free in an existing bed. A city tax of $3 per person per night is added at check-out. Weekend rates are ten percent higher than those shown.
quests.question: How much does breakfast cost per person?
quests.hint: Ignore the room types and look for the extra services.
quests.explanation: Price lists contain many numbers, so match the number to its label. Parking and city tax are near breakfast but cost different amounts.

quests.instruction: Scan the text for the detail you need, then answer.
quests.passage: Fares from Northgate to the coast, standard class: single, $18; day return, $24; open return valid for one month, $33. Off-peak tickets are available after 9:30 a.m. on weekdays and all day at weekends, and cost $6 less than the standard fare. Railcard holders save a third on all tickets except the open return. Children under five travel free, and children aged five to fifteen pay half.
quests.question: What is the price of an off-peak single?
quests.hint: Find the ticket type first, then apply the reduction that goes with it.
quests.explanation: A standard single is $18 and off-peak is $6 cheaper, so $12. Both $18 and $6 are tempting because they appear in the passage.

quests.instruction: Skim the text for the main idea, then answer.
quests.passage: I learned to swim at thirty-four, and I'll admit the first lesson was embarrassing. Standing in the shallow end with a group of eight-year-olds, I wondered whether I had made a terrible mistake. But my instructor was patient, and after a few weeks the fear faded. Now I swim twice a week, and I feel stronger than I did in my twenties. If you have been putting it off, my advice is simple: book the first lesson.
quests.question: What is the writer's attitude to learning to swim as an adult?
quests.hint: Tone shows in the ending. Ask what the writer wants readers to do.
quests.explanation: The writer recommends booking a lesson, so the attitude is encouraging. The early embarrassment is only the start of the story.

quests.instruction: Scan the text for the detail you need, then answer.
quests.passage: Meeting room availability for Thursday. Room A (10 seats): free 9:00 to 11:00 and after 3:00. Room B (20 seats, projector): booked until noon, free from 12:00 to 2:30. Room C (6 seats): free all day except 1:00 to 2:00. Video calls should take place in Room C, which has a soundproof door. Bookings can be cancelled up to one hour before the start, and unused rooms must be left tidy.
quests.question: Which room is free at 1:30?
quests.hint: Check each room's free times against 1:30, one room at a time.
quests.explanation: Room A is busy between 11:00 and 3:00, and Room C is busy from 1:00 to 2:00. Only Room B is free at 1:30.

quests.instruction: Skim the text for the main idea, then answer.
quests.passage: We went to Basilico on a rainy Friday, and we almost left when we saw the queue. I'm glad we stayed. The pasta was fresh, the waiter recommended a wonderful local wine, and the tiramisu was the best I have had outside Italy. The room is small and noisy, and the tables are close together, but that is part of the charm. We paid a little more than expected, though we left happy and are already planning a return visit.
quests.question: How does the writer feel about the restaurant overall?
options: Mostly negative because of the noise
Very positive despite a few small drawbacks
Positive about the price but not the food
quests.correctAnswer: Very positive despite a few small drawbacks
quests.hint: Weigh how the review ends against the complaints in the middle.
quests.explanation: The complaints about noise and price are softened by "part of the charm" and the plan to return. Overall feeling matters more than any single detail.

quests.instruction: Scan the text for the detail you need, then answer.
quests.passage: Children's pain relief syrup. Recommended dose: ages 3 to 5, 5 ml; ages 6 to 8, 7.5 ml; ages 9 to 12, 10 ml. Doses may be repeated every six hours, up to four times in 24 hours. Do not give to children under three without medical advice. Shake well before use and store below 25 degrees. Discard any unused medicine six months after opening.
quests.question: What is the recommended dose for a seven-year-old?
quests.hint: Locate the age band that includes seven before you look at the amounts.
quests.explanation: Seven falls in the 6 to 8 band. The neighbouring bands are the doses most readers mistakenly pick.

quests.instruction: Skim the text for the main idea, then answer.
quests.passage: A new central library opened yesterday after five years of planning and construction. Its bright, open floors include a children's area, quiet study rooms and a small cafe. Hundreds of residents queued to enter, and the mayor described the building as a gift to future generations. Some critics argue the money would have been better spent on more staff, but visitors on opening day seemed delighted.
quests.question: What is the text mostly about?
options: How the cafe inside the library was designed
The opening of a new library and people's reactions
Plans to cut library staff in the coming year
The history of libraries in the city over the years
quests.correctAnswer: The opening of a new library and people's reactions
quests.hint: Ask what every sentence has in common before choosing.
quests.explanation: All the sentences concern the new library and how people responded. Staffing and the cafe are single details.

quests.instruction: Scan the text for the detail you need, then answer.
quests.passage: Route 17. Weekdays: buses leave Harbour Street at 7:05, 7:35, 8:05 and every half hour until 6:05 p.m., with a last bus at 9:00 p.m. Saturdays: first bus 8:00, then hourly until 8:00 p.m. Sundays and public holidays: 10:00, 12:00, 2:00 and 4:00 only. There is no service on 25 December. Buses may run late in heavy traffic, and timetables are displayed at every stop.
quests.question: When is the last bus on Saturdays?
quests.hint: Find the day label first. Times for other days are only noise.
quests.explanation: The Saturday line ends with 8:00 p.m. The 9:00 p.m. bus is a weekday service.

quests.instruction: Skim the text for the main idea, then answer.
quests.passage: Hi all, following last month's survey, we're organising a team-building day in June. Nothing too energetic: some lunch, a short walk and an afternoon quiz. You told us you'd rather not spend a full day away from your desks, so we'll finish by four. Details about location and transport will follow next week. In the meantime, please tell Alice if you have any dietary requirements. Thanks!
quests.question: What is the main purpose of the email?
options: To tell staff about an upcoming team day
To ask staff to complete a survey
quests.correctAnswer: To tell staff about an upcoming team day
quests.hint: Skim for what is being announced, not for the smaller requests.
quests.explanation: The email announces an event and mentions the survey only as the reason for its style. Dietary needs are a small follow-up request.

quests.instruction: Scan the text for the detail you need, then answer.
quests.passage: Vacancies this week. Bakery assistant, Elm Street: 20 hours, $16 per hour, apply by Friday. Delivery driver, Fresh Direct: full-time, $19 per hour, licence required, apply by 15 March. Receptionist, Dr. Lopez's surgery: mornings only, $17 per hour, apply by Tuesday. Library helper, Central Library: 12 hours, volunteer role, no deadline. Contact details are on the notice board.
quests.question: Which job has no application deadline?
quests.hint: Run your eye down the list for the entry that lacks a date or day.
quests.explanation: Three listings say "apply by" and one says "no deadline". Scanning for a missing feature is a useful real-life skill.

quests.instruction: Scan the text for the detail you need, then answer.
quests.passage: Evening courses, spring term. Beginners' Spanish, Mondays 6:30 to 8:00, $95. Digital photography, Wednesdays 7:00 to 9:00, $120, camera required. Creative writing, Tuesdays 6:00 to 7:30, $85. Introduction to bookkeeping, Thursdays 6:30 to 8:30, $140. All courses last eight weeks, and there is a ten percent discount for anyone enrolling in two courses. Enrolment closes a week before each course starts.
quests.question: Which course requires students to bring their own equipment?
quests.hint: Look for a word that signals an obligation next to a course name.
quests.explanation: Only the photography entry says a camera is required. Scanning for a keyword such as "required" is faster than reading every line.

quests.instruction: Skim the text for the main idea, then answer.
quests.passage: Cities keep building wider roads for cars, yet traffic gets worse. Cycling is cheaper, cleaner and quicker over short distances, but many people avoid it because they feel unsafe among lorries and buses. If governments want more people on bikes, they must first give them protected lanes. Encouraging cyclists without protecting them is like inviting guests to a party and then locking the door.
quests.question: What case is the writer making about cycling in cities?
options: Cycling is too dangerous to recommend to anyone
Buses cause most of the traffic problems in cities
Cars should be banned from all city centres
Safe cycle lanes are needed before more people will cycle
quests.correctAnswer: Safe cycle lanes are needed before more people will cycle
quests.hint: The strongest claim usually follows a condition word such as "if".
quests.explanation: The "if governments want... they must first" sentence carries the argument. The party comparison only illustrates it.

quests.instruction: Skim the text for the main idea, then answer.
quests.passage: The TrailLite backpack weighs just 900 grams, yet holds thirty litres. Its waterproof fabric keeps rain out, and the padded straps are designed to stay comfortable on long walks. Multiple pockets keep small items within easy reach, and a hidden compartment protects a phone or wallet. Available in green, grey or orange, it comes with a five-year guarantee.
quests.question: What kind of text is this?
options: A set of assembly instructions for a rucksack
A travel diary about a walking holiday
A product description meant to persuade buyers
A safety warning written for hikers on mountains
quests.correctAnswer: A product description meant to persuade buyers
quests.hint: Decide from the features and the closing offer, not from any single number.
quests.explanation: Listing benefits and ending with a guarantee is typical of selling a product. Skimming for text type is faster than reading each feature.

quests.instruction: Scan the text for the detail you need, then answer.
quests.passage: Baggage allowance by fare. Basic fare: one cabin bag up to 8 kg, no checked baggage. Standard fare: one cabin bag and one checked bag up to 20 kg. Flex fare: one cabin bag and two checked bags up to 23 kg each. Extra checked bags cost $40 online or $55 at the airport. Sports equipment such as skis is charged at $30 on all fares. Bags over the limit pay $12 per extra kilogram.
quests.question: How much does an extra checked bag cost if it is booked online?
quests.hint: Two prices are given for the same thing. Which condition does the question mention?
quests.explanation: The online price is $40 and the airport price $55. Skis and overweight charges are different items.

quests.instruction: Scan the text for the detail you need, then answer.
quests.passage: Vegetable soup, serves four. You will need two carrots, one large onion, three potatoes, a stick of celery, one litre of vegetable stock, two tablespoons of olive oil, and salt and pepper. Chop the vegetables, soften the onion in oil for five minutes, add everything else and simmer for 25 minutes. Blend if you prefer a smooth soup. Serve with bread.
quests.question: How long should the soup simmer?
quests.hint: Find the cooking verb, then read the time attached to it.
quests.explanation: Five minutes is for softening the onion, while simmering takes 25. Numbers cluster in recipes, so tie each to its action.

quests.instruction: Skim the text for the main idea, then answer.
quests.passage: I have been a customer of your store for over ten years and have never before felt the need to complain. However, my experience last Saturday was very disappointing. I waited twenty minutes to be served, the assistant did not apologise, and the jacket I bought had a broken zip. I would like a replacement or a refund, and I hope standards can return to what they used to be.
quests.question: What is the writer's tone?
quests.hint: Judge the tone from how the writer opens and closes, not from the number of problems.
quests.explanation: The writer praises long loyalty, lists problems calmly and asks for a fix. That is disappointment without rudeness.

quests.instruction: Skim the text for the main idea, then answer.
quests.passage: Temperatures across the region are expected to reach forty degrees this week, the highest for a decade. Health officials urge residents to drink plenty of water, avoid strenuous activity in the afternoon and check on elderly neighbours. Schools will shorten their days, and some outdoor events have been cancelled. Forecasters say cooler air should arrive by the weekend, bringing possible thunderstorms.
quests.question: What is the main topic of the text?
options: Advice and arrangements during extreme heat
How weather has changed over ten years
quests.correctAnswer: Advice and arrangements during extreme heat
quests.hint: Group the details: warnings, closures, forecast. What do they share?
quests.explanation: Every detail relates to coping with a heatwave. Thunderstorms and school hours are only single points.

quests.instruction: Scan the text for the detail you need, then answer.
quests.passage: Mobile plans. Lite: 5 GB data, 200 minutes, $12 a month. Plus: 20 GB, unlimited minutes, $22. Max: 60 GB, unlimited minutes and texts, roaming in Europe included, $35. All plans require an eighteen-month contract, but Lite can be changed to Plus at any time. New customers get a free phone case, and Max customers also receive three months of music streaming.
quests.question: Which plan gives unlimited minutes at the lowest price?
quests.hint: Cross out any plan without unlimited minutes first, then compare what is left.
quests.explanation: Lite has only 200 minutes, so it is out. Plus and Max both have unlimited minutes, and Plus is cheaper.

quests.instruction: Scan the text for the detail you need, then answer.
quests.passage: Third-floor flat, Linden Road: two bedrooms, a modern kitchen and a small balcony facing the park. Rent $1,150 a month; deposit equal to one month's rent. Heating included, electricity extra. Fifteen minutes' walk to the station, five to the supermarket. Cats allowed with the owner's approval. Bicycles can be stored in the courtyard. Available from 1 February. Viewings on Saturday morning by appointment.
quests.question: How much is the deposit?
quests.hint: A deposit is defined by comparison with something else in the ad.
quests.explanation: The deposit equals one month's rent, which is $1,150. You must connect two phrases rather than find a number labelled "deposit."

quests.instruction: Read the text quickly and answer the question.
quests.passage: Arrivals, Terminal 2. AB 302 from Madrid, 14:10, landed. KL 771 from Amsterdam, 14:25, delayed to 15:05, Belt 4. LX 640 from Zurich, 14:40, on time, Belt 2. BA 118 from London, 15:00, on time, Belt 6. TP 205 from Lisbon, 15:15, cancelled. Passengers on delayed flights will receive a snack voucher at Desk 9. Please check the screens for gate changes.
quests.question: Which belt will passengers from Amsterdam use?
quests.hint: Match the city, then read to the end of that entry.
quests.explanation: The Amsterdam flight is KL 771, and its entry ends with Belt 4. Desk 9 is where vouchers are given, not a baggage belt.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: Parents often worry about how much time children spend on screens, but researchers say the amount matters less than what children are doing. Watching videos alone for hours is different from video-calling grandparents or building a game. Experts recommend that families agree on clear rules, such as no phones at meals, and that adults follow the same rules. Children copy what they see far more than what they hear.
quests.question: Which idea best sums up the text?
options: Children should never be allowed to use screens
Video calls are harmful for young people
Rules about meals are pointless for families
The type of screen use and adult example matter most
quests.correctAnswer: The type of screen use and adult example matter most
quests.hint: Notice which claim the writer sets against "the amount".
quests.explanation: The text moves attention from quantity to quality and to parental example. Extreme options such as "never" are not supported.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Missing: Biscuit, a brown and white spaniel, last seen on Saturday evening near Green Lane Park. He is friendly but nervous around traffic and wears a red collar with a bell. Please do not chase him; call Mr. Farouk on 555-0139 or bring him to the vet on Mill Road, which has offered to scan his microchip. A reward of $100 is offered for his safe return.
quests.question: Where can the dog be taken to have his microchip checked?
quests.hint: A specific service word points you to one place in the notice.
quests.explanation: The vet is the only place said to scan a microchip. The park is where he was last seen.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: When I first arrived in Toronto, everything felt too big: the streets, the buildings, even the supermarkets. I missed my mother's cooking and the sound of my own language. Slowly, though, small things changed. A neighbour invited me to dinner, a colleague taught me to skate, and one morning I realised I had stopped counting the days until my flight home.
quests.question: What experience is the writer describing in Toronto?
options: Gradually feeling at home in a new place
Missing a family recipe from home
Learning to skate with a colleague
The cost of living in a large Canadian city
quests.correctAnswer: Gradually feeling at home in a new place
quests.hint: Look for the turning point in the story and where it leads.
quests.explanation: The writer moves from feeling lost to feeling settled. Skating and cooking are examples, not the point.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Membership rates. Adult: $360 a year or $35 monthly. Student (with ID): $210 a year. Senior (over 65): $250 a year. Family (two adults and up to three children): $640. A joining fee of $40 applies to all new members except students. Payment by monthly instalments is available only for adult memberships. Guests can play for $8 per visit, up to three times a year.
quests.question: Which group does NOT pay the joining fee?
quests.hint: Scan for the word that introduces an exception.
quests.explanation: "Except students" removes them from the fee. Every other group in the list pays it.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: After three months, I still love this vacuum cleaner. It is light, quiet and picks up pet hair that my old machine simply pushed around. The battery lasts about forty minutes, which is enough for my flat, and emptying the bin takes two seconds. My only complaint is that the charging cable is short, so the machine has to be stored near a socket. I would definitely recommend it.
quests.question: What does the reviewer think of the product?
options: It is very good, apart from one small problem
It is disappointing overall and not worth buying
It is too loud for use in small flats
It is average and rather expensive for what it does
quests.correctAnswer: It is very good, apart from one small problem
quests.hint: Count how many criticisms there are, then look at the last sentence.
quests.explanation: One minor complaint and a clear recommendation show a strongly positive view. The machine is described as quiet.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Annual Language Teachers' Conference, Saturday programme. 9:00 registration and coffee. 9:30 opening address by Dr. Ilse Braun. 10:15 Workshop A, Games in the classroom (Room 1), or Workshop B, Teaching with podcasts (Room 3). 11:45 break. 12:15 panel discussion, The future of exams. 1:00 lunch in the atrium. 2:00 poster session. 3:30 closing remarks. Certificates of attendance are available at the desk after 3:30.
quests.question: Where is the workshop about podcasts held?
quests.hint: Match the topic word to its workshop letter, then to a room.
quests.explanation: Workshop B covers podcasts and meets in Room 3. Room 1 hosts the games workshop.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: A survey of five thousand workers found that nearly half now spend at least one day a week working from home, up from one in five before 2020. Most said they were more productive, but a quarter reported feeling lonely. Employers are responding with occasional office days and social events, while some companies have reduced the size of their offices to save money.
quests.question: Which title suits the text best?
options: Workers Prefer Loneliness to Commuting Every Day
Employers Ban Home Working for Good
Offices Are Closing Across the Whole Country
Home Working Is Growing, With Benefits and Drawbacks
quests.correctAnswer: Home Working Is Growing, With Benefits and Drawbacks
quests.hint: A good title covers both the trend and the mixed reaction to it.
quests.explanation: The text reports growth in home working, higher productivity and loneliness. Office downsizing is only mentioned in passing.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: Tickets for the Summer Music Festival are non-refundable, but they can be transferred to another person until 48 hours before the event. To transfer, log in and enter the new holder's name and email; a fee of $5 applies. If the festival is cancelled, all tickets will be refunded automatically within 30 days. In case of bad weather, the festival will go ahead unless the authorities advise otherwise.
quests.question: Under what condition will ticket holders get their money back?
quests.hint: Ask which sentence contains an actual promise of money, and what triggers it.
quests.explanation: Only cancellation of the festival triggers a refund. Bad weather does not, and transfers cost a fee.
